execucoes.pergunta: What is the recommended treatment for P001's diabetes?
protocolos_recuperados: Protocol ID: PR001, Title: Diabetes Management Guidelines
Protocol ID: PR015, Title: Diabetic Foot Care Guidelines
Protocol ID: PR002, Title: Hypertension Treatment Pathway
execucoes.resposta_entregue: The recommended treatment for P001s diabetes is metformin. Metformin, a biguanide medication, prevents cells in the liver from making too much glucose and helps cells in the muscles and liver take up more glucose. Metformin is also an insulin sensitizer medication, which means it helps the body respond to its own insulin. Metformin is taken by mouth and is absorbed by the intestine. For an average weight adult, the recommended starting dose is 500 milligrams (mg) twice a day with meals. The dose is often increased by 500 mg each week until a successful blood glucose level is reached. The maintenance dose is usually 1000-2000 mg per day in divided doses. Blood glucose levels should be monitored every 1-2 months.

execucoes.pergunta: P003 has coronary artery disease. Should I prescribe them a new medication?
protocolos_recuperados: Protocol ID: PR011, Title: Cardiovascular Risk Assessment
Protocol ID: PR006, Title: GERD Management Guidelines
Protocol ID: PR010, Title: Post-Pneumonia Follow-up
execucoes.resposta_entregue: Yes. Statins (such as Atorvastatin) are usually the first line of therapy for treating coronary artery disease. They help lower your LDL (bad) cholesterol levels and the risk of heart attacks. If your LDL level is still above 100 mg/dL, you may need to try a different statin. Doctors will check your LDL level every 3 to 12 months to see if you need to change your cholesterol-lowering medication.
